## NEUTROPENIC ENTEROCOLITIS (TYPHLITIS)
Oral step-down treatment
Neutropenic enterocolitis, also known as "typhlitis" or "necrotizing
enterocolitis", is a severe intraabdominal infection that occurs in neutropenic
patients, especially in those with acute leukemia.
Send stool for C. difficile testing to exclude of C. difficile infection.
[Clostridioides difficile infection](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)
Hematology-oncology, Infectious Diseases and general surgery consults are
essential.
Broad spectrum antimicrobials that include anaerobic coverage should be
initiated promptly.
## Duration of antimicrobial therapy
Continue antimicrobial therapy until normalization of body temperature, recovery
of neutropenia (unless planning to transition back to antimicrobial
prophylaxis), recovery of thrombocytopenia, return of normal gastrointestinal
function and resolution of bacteremia if initially present. Infectious Disease
consult recommended to guide duration if perforation, abscess, or other
complicating feature present.
## Treatment
## Inpatient

Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]
< OR >
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
## Alternative
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
